主要内容: Biotech and small drug companies are rarely acquired immediately before or after a drug approval or during the initial phase of a new drug launch. Vivus, which is awaiting FDA approval for its weight-loss drug Qnexa, may be in secret negotiations with a Big Pharma suitor. However, such a deal would be unusual. More likely, Vivus will launch the drug independently, and if sales boom, a suitor may come calling. Similar patterns are seen in past acquisitions, where biotech firms are typically acquired during mid- to late-stage clinical trials or after drug approval. Examples include Roche buying Inhibitex and Gilead Sciences acquiring Pharmasset. Other notable deals include Johnson & Johnson buying Cougar Biotech and Amgen acquiring Micromet. Companies like Eli Lilly and Takeda Pharmaceutical acquired firms after their drugs had years of sales. Forest Laboratories bought Clinical Data weeks after its antidepressant Viibryd received FDA approval. Amylin Pharmaceuticals, which recently launched Bydureon, also reportedly spurned a takeout offer from Bristol-Myers Squibb. These examples suggest that drug companies are often acquired after commercial launch, not during early stages of product development.
